Struggle for existence and natural selection

These two chapters are a piece of arithmetic before they are biology. Every species produces more young than can possibly survivep. 61, so in every generation most die before they breed. Darwin calls the competition that follows the struggle for existence, and says he uses the phrase “in a large and metaphorical sense”: a plant on the edge of a desert struggles against drought as much as against other plants.p. 62

From that, one step follows. If any variation gives its owner even a slight advantage, its owner is more likely to survive and leave young, and the young tend to inherit it.

“This preservation of favourable variations and the rejection of injurious variations, I call Natural Selection.”p. 81

Three ideas to hold

  • Geometrical increase. Numbers would multiply without limit if nothing checked them.
  • Checks fall on the young. Most lives end early, from food, weather, enemies or disease.
  • Small differences add up. Selection works on every part, all the time, over immense spans.p. 84

Key terms

Struggle for existence
Darwin's name for every check on survival, not only fighting.
Natural selection
The keeping of useful variations and the loss of harmful ones.
Divergence of character
Descendants spread into different ways of life, so differences grow.
